business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Catalog Retail of Industrial Maintenance Hardware

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Federal Common Law superimposed on Quebec Civil Law (RLRQ) governing private and corporate matters; Quebec is a mixed civil-law jurisdiction for corporate obligations and property rights.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CUSMA (Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement), in force July 1, 2020
CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership), in force for Canada December 30, 2018
CETA (Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement), provisionally applied September 21, 2017
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force April 1, 2021
Canada–United States Income Tax Convention (1980), as amended by Protocols (active DTAA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended (PCMLTFA); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.3; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 45; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2017, c 21; Quebec Business Corporations Act, RLRQ c S-31.1, ss 25–33; Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons, RLRQ c P-44.1; Quebec Regulation respecting the declaration of information on persons exercising control (UBO declaration regime); FINTRAC Regulations, SOR/2002-412; Global Affairs Canada Authentication and Apostille Services (effective in Canada January 11, 2024).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution / Attestation de constitution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada (Ottawa)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Status (Attestation d'état de la personne morale)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized By-laws and Organizational Resolutions (Règlements internes et résolutions constitutives)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary (public officer) or licensed Quebec lawyer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; or Consular Legalization via Canadian Embassy/Consulate for non-Hague destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Déclaration de renseignements sur les personnes occupant un poste de contrôle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada (when required by a foreign competent authority or regulated financial institution)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate Power of Attorney / Mandate (Procuration / Mandat)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; or Consular Legalization (non-Hague destination)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding 25% or more, and authorized representatives against: (i) FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) categories under PCMLTFA ss 11.12–11.13, covering domestic PEPs, foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their immediate family and close associates; (ii) OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions; (iii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) Canadian consolidated sanctions list maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (v) RCMP and global PEP databases. Screening must occur at onboarding and continuously on a rolling 24-hour basis using automated sanctions/PEP monitoring tools; enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth verification are required for any positive PEP hit or high-risk jurisdiction nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Registre des entreprises en ligne (online corporate register; www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca); federal alternative: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre (for CBCA incorporations, if the entity elects federal articles with Quebec extra-provincial registration).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (RLRQ c C-11), the corporate name must be in French and the legal designation must be French ('inc.', 'corp.', 'ltée', 'incorporée', 'corporation', 'limitée'). A non-French version may accompany the French name but may not replace it. Non-Roman script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and registered in that transliterated French form. The REQ rejects names that are English-only, misleading as to legal form, or contrary to French-language norms.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens implying Crown or government connection: 'Canada', 'Québec', 'Federal', 'Royal', 'Municipal', 'Police'
Tokens implying regulated financial activity: 'Bank'/'Banque', 'Insurance'/'Assurance', 'Trust'/'Fiduciaire', 'Loan'/'Prêt', 'Broker'/'Courtier', 'Securities'/'Valeurs mobilières'
Tokens requiring prior ministerial or professional order authorization: 'University'/'Université', 'College'/'Collège', 'Chamber of Commerce', 'Order'/'Ordre professionnel'
Tokens that are misleading, offensive, contrary to public order, or falsely suggest a nonprofit or cooperative status
Names that are confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise name or a distinctive trademark protected in Quebec
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a REQ name rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal, attaching revised name alternatives and legal arguments; (2) if reconsideration is denied, initiate a judicial review application in the Superior Court of Quebec (Code of Civil Procedure, RLRQ c C-25.01, arts 529 et seq.) within 30 days of the reconsideration decision; or (3) alternatively, incorporate under a numbered name and later apply to the REQ for a name change once a cleared name is obtained. Standard processing timelines: REQ reconsideration 15–30 business days; Superior Court review 3–6 months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk B2B MRO electronic catalog retailer, provided the registered office is a physical street address in Quebec where the corporation's statutory records and minute book are kept and where legal process can be served; post-office boxes are not acceptable. Virtual-office or registered-agent arrangements are commonly accepted by the REQ, but the company must maintain an appointed registered agent and production-ready corporate records in Quebec.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: <5% probability per fiscal year for a low-risk, unlicensed e-commerce MRO supplier; 10–15% probability if the AML risk tier is upgraded by a financial institution or if FINTRAC initiates a compliance examination pursuant to PCMLTFA s 64.1; the REQ also performs random address-validity correspondence checks, but unannounced physical premises inspections are rare for this industry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation application (demande de réservation de nom) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Quebec Regulation respecting fees payable under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c P-44.1, r 2)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and initial registration declaration for a Quebec business corporation (CA_CORP)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government filing tariff (approx CAD 351; prevailing REQ schedule)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration of persons exercising control (poste de contrôle)
Legal drafting of Articles, By-laws, organizational resolutions, and UBO/PEP compliance policy (fixed-fee corporate package)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — fixed fee for standard QBCA incorporation package (CAD 250–450/hr equivalent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille authentication bundle for five corporate documents (Global Affairs Canada fee CAD 30 per document plus notary attendance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary and Global Affairs Canada (Authentication and Apostille Services)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authentication fee plus prevailing notarial tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Automated PEP and international sanctions screening subscription (continuous 24-hour monitoring of directors, officers, UBOs, and counterparties)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party AML compliance screening vendor (e.g., World-Check / Dow Jones / LexisNexis)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market subscription benchmark (annual per-entity SaaS fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and virtual office arrangement in Quebec (12-month service, physical address for service of process and records)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CAD 250–500 per annum for standard virtual office)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate minute book, seals, and statutory records kit (optional but recommended)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 6 (contents of Articles), 22 (registered office in Quebec), 30-33 (certificate of constitution), 44 (first directors), 45-52 (share capital and no-par shares), 79 (directors' powers), 102-123 (officers); Act respecting the Legal Publicity of Enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 8-16 (registration and annual declarations); Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 296-307 (legal persons).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Registrar of Enterprises) — one-stop shop 'Entreprises Quebec' online portal; certificate of constitution is issued electronically by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts de constitution / Articles of Incorporation (Form 3), accompanied by the Application Form (Form 1); executed in French or bilingual form and filed via the Registrar's electronic filing service (Portail des services en ligne).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital applies under the QBCA; authorized capital may consist of shares without par value issued for cash, property, services or promissory notes (s. 46 QBCA). No escrow account is required at incorporation; the full subscription price is reflected in the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec on [Date] are adopted; 2. the authorized capital of the Company shall be an unlimited number of Common and Preferred Shares without par value; 3. the Company hereby allots and issues [Number] Common Shares to each incorporator at CAD $[Amount] per share, paid in cash, and the share register is ordered accordingly; 4. the registered office is established at [Street Address], [City], Quebec H0A 0A0, where the statutory registers shall be kept; 5. [Director A] and [Director B] are ratified as directors; 6. [Name] is appointed President and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, with the power to sign corporate documents and open bank accounts; 7. completion of tax registration, municipal licensing and environmental compliance filings is authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec — name analysis service (Analyse de denomination), available online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Registraire's online service; enter up to three proposed French or bilingual legal names reflecting the NAICS 423840 activity (e.g., 'Fournitures MRO Industrielles QC Inc.'); pay the applicable name analysis tariff; upon approval, the name is reserved for 90 days. Without a reserved name, incorporators may file using the legal name 'NEQ number Quebec Inc.'.
required_dossiers: Brief description of principal activity (ISIC 4791 / NAICS 423840)
List of existing registrations if claiming distinction
Client signed authorization if filing by a third-party agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the name, file a new variation within 15 days or submit an explanatory brief distinguishing the trademark; the Registrar may allow cohabitation where goods/services classes differ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing of Articles of Incorporation and issuance of certificate of constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec — online incorporation module (Portail des services en ligne).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the incorporation module; choose 'Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA)'; fill in the enterprise name, head office address in Quebec, share structure (classes, rights, restrictions), first directors (or declaration that incorporators will name them), predominant language of management (French), and any restrictions; confirm the declaration; pay the CAD 200 fee by credit card or SWIFT/wire; sign electronically; receive the immediate certificate of constitution and the NEQ permanent identification number.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form 3) with model clauses
Consents of the first directors, if named in the articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the application is placed under review, the Registrar issues a notice of request for correction; cure by amending the electronic form and refiling within the correction period; no substantive delays accumulate beyond 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational meeting — first board resolution, registered office and issuance of shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office (corporate records), duly minuted and, if desired, notarized by a Quebec notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators or first directors convene a board meeting; adopt the first board resolution (as presented in the legal framework); sign the notice of establishment of registered office; effect the allotment and issuance of shares; record subscriptions in the shareholders' register; elect officers; insert the by-laws or defer adoption to the first shareholders' meeting; verify the electronic commerce franchise and the low-risk anti-money-laundering classification.
required_dossiers: Share subscription list, share certificates and register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: An organizational defect is ratified ex post by unanimous shareholder consent pursuant to s. 177 QBCA; corrected minutes may be signed retrospectively by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GST/QST, payroll and corporate income tax registration with Revenu Quebec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec Centre de services aux entreprises and Canada Revenue Agency — integrated New Business Registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the NEQ is received, complete the one-stop business registration: register for federal GST (5%) and Quebec QST (9.975%) accounts for the retail catalog sales; open a payroll deduction account (income tax, QPP, QPIP, HSF) with Revenu Quebec; file the corporate income tax election (fiscal year end); receive the business number (BN) and RC/RT/RM account numbers; identify the beneficial owner and directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revenu Quebec may backdate registration if filings are late; administrative penalties are cancelled upon voluntary disclosure (Programme de divulgation volontaire) before any enforcement notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal establishment permit and environmental/compliance pre-clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal permits office (e.g., Acces Montreal / Service des permis et inspections) and, where applicable, MELCCFP regional office for pre-authorization confirmation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the business establishment/occupancy permit for the warehouse and office; include the lease, premises plan, and fire safety classification; confirm zoning permits e-commerce/warehousing; for MRO goods storage, complete the regulated-materials self-assessment; maintain the administrative file for later inspection.
required_dossiers: Copy of lease title and attestation of authorized use
Premises layout plan and fire safety certificate
Self-declaration of absence of listed contaminating activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal to the municipal council within 30 days of the refusal letter; alternatively submit a commissioning and environmental compliance plan to address the stated deficiency; the final judicial remedy lies with the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (TAQ) for municipal matters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Service des permis et inspections of the local Quebec municipality, in coordination with the Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ) for building safety assessments; no provincial occupational license is required for electronic catalog retail (ISIC 4791) of industrial MRO hardware, but the physical warehouse and commercial occupation are subject to municipal permitting.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'etablissement commercial (Business Establishment Permit) — 'commerce de detail en ligne et entreposage de fournitures de maintenance industrielle'; additional 'Permis d'entreposage de matieres dangereuses' if flammable or regulated MRO products (lubricants, aerosols, solvents) are stocked above exemption thresholds.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction regionale de l'evaluation environnementale (Quebec).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory EIA: the catalog e-commerce retail and warehousing activity is not listed in the mandatory evaluation schedule of the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2); a negative 'certificat d'autorisation' is not required unless construction works trigger building permits; a voluntary 'attestation d'exemption' may be obtained for the client's due diligence file.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater: only sanitary discharge compliant with municipal sewer by-law (limits typically 300 mg/L BOD5, 300 mg/L suspended solids, pH 6.0-9.5, grease 15 mg/L for cafeteria effluent); VOC reporting threshold of 10 tonnes/year per facility under the Reglement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphere; storage of bulk products conforms to the Quebec Safety Code (Ch. I, Batiment) and flammable liquids standards; hazardous waste manifests (RAULR/CALR) apply where solvents and oils are discarded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory fire safety inspection certificate issued by the municipal fire safety department (Service de securite incendie) before opening; building and racking designed to the Code de construction du Quebec and NFPA 13 sprinkler standards where required; CNESST employer registration, first-aid kit, emergency response plan, and workplace clearance certificate for the warehouse; security plan, WHMIS pictograms, and SDS binders for any controlled MRO products.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada for federal GST/HST and federal income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec provincial corporate income tax, and employer source deductions; Registraire d'entreprises du Québec for provincial business registration. Primary online portals: CRA Business Registration Online, CRA My Business Account, and Revenu Québec Mon dossier d'entreprise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor typically forms a Canadian corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act. The corporation then obtains a federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) through the CRA Business Registration Online service, providing articles of incorporation, registered office address, director information, and board authorization. GST/HST program account (RT), payroll, and other program accounts are activated in the same process. A separate Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) is issued by the Registraire d'entreprises du Québec, and the corporation must register for QST and provincial payroll accounts through the Revenu Québec online registration service. A foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Canada may apply for a simplified non-resident registration using CRA Form RC4591 and, for Quebec, the equivalent Revenu Québec registration procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxable legal entity. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment. Resident Canadian corporations are subject to Canadian federal and provincial income tax on worldwide income. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada are subject to Canadian tax on Canadian-source income and to Part I Part XII.1 branch tax where applicable. No tax-exempt zone applies. A small supplier may be exempt from mandatory registration, but this is a registration threshold, not an entity-level tax exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box tax classification election exists under Canadian tax law. Corporate tax status follows the entity's legal form. Available elections include the section 85(1)/(2) asset rollover election for incorporation or business restructuring; the Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status election; the GST/HST Quick Method election for small suppliers; the annual GST/HST filing election for non-resident registrants; the closely related corporation election to relieve certain GST/HST obligations; the section 216(4) election for non-residents to compute Canadian rental income on a net basis; and corresponding Quebec tax elections administered by Revenu Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.explicit_policy_note_by_model: This dossier adopts the legal tax classification of the entity structure supplied in the task payload; no additional factual assumptions are introduced.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST); in Quebec the federal GST rate is 5% and the provincial QST rate is 9.5%, producing a combined headline consumption-tax rate of 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. Under both the Excise Tax Act (GST/HST) and Quebec's QST Act, a person is a small supplier unless the total value of its worldwide taxable supplies from Canada and elsewhere exceeds CAD 30,000 in a particular calendar quarter and in the four preceding calendar quarters. Non-resident vendors making taxable supplies of digital services or intangible property to Canadian consumers may be required to register if the threshold is met or exceeded. Quebec applies substantially the same CAD 30,000 threshold for QST registration. There is no monetary threshold for a non-resident that carries on business in Canada through a permanent establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently operate a continuous transaction control (CTC) regime. There is no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no government digital stamping, and no API pre-clearance requirement for standard B2B invoices. Suppliers must issue invoices containing the prescribed statutory information: supplier and recipient identities, the supplier's GST/HST registration number and Quebec QST registration number where applicable, invoice date, description of goods/services, VAT/GST/QST amounts, rates, and total amount. Electronic invoices in PDF, EDI, or other machine-readable formats are accepted, but the issuer must retain an auditable copy in Canada for at least six years. Quebec has been advancing mandatory electronic invoicing in phases for established large enterprises, but as of the current stage no QR-code or real-time fiscal approval requirement applies to an industrial MRO electronic-catalog seller.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to GST/HST and QST when goods are exported from Canada and ownership in the goods passes to a non-resident buyer, provided the goods are exported as part of the supply, or are delivered to a common carrier for export, or otherwise removed from Canada in accordance with Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and the corresponding Quebec QST rules. Services are zero-rated where the supply is made to a non-resident and the service is performed wholly outside Canada, subject to exceptions for services relating to real property in Canada, tangible personal property located in Canada, or services performed in Canada that are not expressly listed as zero-rated. The supplier must retain documentary evidence of export; without that evidence the supply becomes taxable at the standard rates, and the supplier must account for GST/HST and QST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency export declaration or Canada Customs coding form)
Bill of Lading (original transport document or equivalent ocean/air/rail/road waybill)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 proof of payment from the non-resident buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the exported goods
Cargo control document or carrier-issued export evidence
Customs broker exporter summary or freight forwarder invoice
Proof of foreign destination and delivery, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec actively verify zero-rated export claims, especially for high-volume e-commerce sellers. If the exporter cannot produce satisfactory written evidence of export and payment, the tax authority will reassess the supply as taxable, disallow the zero-rating, and assess unreported GST/HST and QST plus statutory interest. For fraudulent or grossly negligent claims, the Excise Tax Act authorizes a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 500 and 25% of the net amount of tax sought to be evaded, and Revenu Québec imposes a comparable civil penalty. Criminal tax evasion is also prosecutable. The normal four-year reassessment window is extended to eight years where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established. Refund offsets and criminal fines may apply in the most serious cases.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.specific_mro_ecommerce_note: For ISIC 4791 electronic-catalog sales of industrial maintenance hardware, zero-rating eligibility will be assessed on a transaction-by-transaction basis. Clean evidence of actual physical export is mandatory; documentation generated solely for customs-warehousing, drop-shipping, or freight-forwarding without proof of final foreign consignee may be rejected.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates a free convertibility regime for current account transactions pursuant to the Bank of Canada Act. Capital account transactions are convertible subject to reporting obligations to Statistics Canada. Profit remittances by Canadian corporations are unrestricted for most sectors, subject only to tax withholding, FINTRAC compliance, and beneficial ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank is required. Canadian exporters must file export declarations with Statistics Canada through the Export Reporting System within 45 days of shipment. Proceeds may be retained offshore or repatriated freely without central bank conversion mandates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border digital payment platforms and electronic money instruments via licensed providers such as Wise Business or Revolut Business. Legal constraints include mandatory FINTRAC registration for money services businesses and OSFI oversight for any EMI activities; offshore digital EMIs require full compliance with Canadian AML/KYC standards and may face remittance restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is fully permitted for Canadian corporations. Video KYC and director interviews are mandatory; physical presence is not required except in cases of high-value transactions or complex beneficial ownership structures where enhanced due diligence may necessitate in-person verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or PEP screening adverse hits on directors, officers, or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions clearance certificates, source-of-funds affidavits, independent background verification reports, and legal opinions confirming no adverse findings

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media or negative news coverage linked to principals
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive media monitoring reports, corporate registry extracts, and third-party due diligence summaries demonstrating clean history

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent or incomplete beneficial ownership disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date corporate registry filings, shareholder agreements, and notarized declarations of ownership percentages

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are executed via SWIFT wire transfers using purpose codes such as 'Capital Contribution', 'Equity Injection', or 'Share Capital'. All wires require supporting documentation including board resolutions, incorporation certificates, and valuation reports. Verification is conducted under FINTRAC and OSFI guidelines with real-time screening for sanctions and ML/TF risks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers and Commercial Letters of Credit for structured trade finance. Correspondent banking networks enable direct clearing with global partners. All disbursements must include accurate purpose codes and supporting trade documentation to satisfy export reporting and AML obligations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the date of the annual shareholders' meeting; if the meeting is dispensed with, within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative monetary penalty for late filing; after two consecutive years of default the corporation may be dissolved under CBCA s. 212, and directors may be personally liable for obligations incurred while the corporation is unlawful.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update Declaration (Annual Renewal) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year of the corporation; changes to recorded information must additionally be filed within 30 days of the event, including transfers of shares affecting significant control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under the Legal Publicity Act; persistent failure may lead to the cancellation of the enterprise registration by the REQ and loss of corporate capacity to carry on activities in Quebec.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; balance of tax due is payable by the second month after year-end (third month for a Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the small business deduction).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of balance due up to 12 months; a higher penalty applies for recidivist non-filing; CRA may issue a demand and prosecute directors under the trust fund rules for unremitted source deductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end; provincial balance due is payable by the third month after year-end for eligible CCPCs and the second month otherwise.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty, interest, and administrative fines imposed by Revenu Québec under the Taxation Act; the minister may require a security and, in serious cases, prosecute directors for deficient remittances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A distributing corporation (publicly traded) must appoint an independent auditor. For a non-distributing private corporation, the appointment of an auditor can be dispensed with by unanimous shareholder consent annually; no revenue, asset, or employee thresholds make a non-distributing private corporation compulsory-audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB for publicly accountable enterprises; private enterprises may apply Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE / CPA Canada Handbook Part II). Quebec corporations use CPA Canada Handbook standards for financial reporting where an audit or review is prepared.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A register of individuals with significant control (ISC) must be maintained and updated within 15 days of the corporation becoming aware of a share transfer or other event changing significant control. The Quebec annual update declaration must identify each individual with significant control as of the fiscal year end and is the annual confirmation vehicle; no separate standalone federal annual UBO return is filed apart from the CBCA annual return's declaration on ISC register currency.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to 12,000 per year for a small private corporation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (15% federal general corporate rate + 11.5% Quebec general corporate rate)
